changes.title: Phase 1: Registry domain
changes.why:
Every later part of Spotter (serving, drift monitoring, shadow testing, promotion, rollback) needs one answer to "which model versions exist, where are their artifacts, and which one is live?" That answer has to be strict. A boolean `is_active` can't tell a version that was never validated apart from one that was rolled back, and it can't stop a rejected version from going live. The version lifecycle has to be an explicit state machine, enforced in plain code and in the database, before anything is allowed to act on it.

The registry is also the first service built in the hexagonal layout every Go service follows. Its domain and use-case code must not depend on Postgres, so the boundary is checked by a test from the first commit.
changes.what_changes:
- Add the registry's domain: models, model versions with a verifiable artifact (S3 URI, SHA-256, framework, metrics), and the version lifecycle as a table of allowed stage transitions.
- Add use cases: register a model, register a version (numbered sequentially per model), transition a version's stage with a reason and an expected revision, and read versions and their history.
- Enforce "at most one production version per model" in the database and report it as a domain error.
- Detect concurrent transitions of the same version with optimistic concurrency (a revision number) and reject the stale one.
- Write an event for every registration and stage change to a transactional outbox, in the same transaction as the change. Event payloads are protobuf messages defined in `proto/`. Publishing them comes in a later change.
- Add two repository adapters, PostgreSQL and in-memory, that pass one shared contract test suite.
- Add the registry process: configuration from environment variables, migrations at startup, liveness and readiness endpoints, and graceful shutdown.
- Add the Go spec-to-test convention and a coverage check that fails the build when a requirement has no passing test.
- Add a test that fails the build if domain, port, or use-case code imports infrastructure.

changes.title: Phase 2: Registry API
changes.why: The registry's use cases exist but nothing outside the process can call them. The trainer needs to register versions, operators need to move versions through stages, and later the inference worker needs to find the production version. Other services need a typed, versioned contract (gRPC); people and simple tools need plain HTTP and JSON. Both have to come from one definition so they can't drift apart.
changes.what_changes:
- Add `spotter.v1.RegistryService` in `proto/spotter/v1/registry.proto`: register and get models; register, get, list, and transition versions; read a version's history. REST paths are declared on each RPC in the same file.
- Serve the API over gRPC from the registry, with the standard gRPC health service and server reflection.
- Map every registry error to one gRPC status code, in one place. Validation errors carry the name of the offending field as a structured error detail.
- Add the gateway service, the public HTTP front door. It translates REST/JSON requests into registry gRPC calls, returns errors as JSON with the matching HTTP status, and serves an OpenAPI document generated from the protobuf definitions.
- Add `GRPC_ADDR` to the registry's configuration, and stop the gRPC server gracefully on shutdown.

changes.title: Phase 3: Model training
changes.why: The registry can store model versions, but there is no model yet. Everything after this (serving, optimization, drift monitoring, shadow testing) needs a real trained classifier with honestly measured accuracy, an artifact that can be verified byte for byte, and enough recorded context to reproduce it. Training also has to be disciplined from the start: a holdout set that training never touches, and metrics that report per-class weaknesses rather than one flattering number.
changes.what_changes:
- Add a shared Python package with the EuroSAT classifier architecture, the class list, and the image preprocessing, so training and serving can never disagree on them.
- Add the trainer: download and verify EuroSAT, split it deterministically and stratified by class into train, validation, and holdout sets, train a small CNN on the CPU, and evaluate it on the holdout set once training ends.
- Add evaluation metrics: accuracy, per-class precision and recall, macro F1, and the confusion matrix.
- Publish each trained model to the object store under a key derived from its SHA-256, with a metadata file recording the data split hash, seed, hyperparameters, code commit, library versions, and metrics.
- Register the version with the registry over gRPC with its holdout metrics, creating the model if it doesn't exist, and move it to `validated` only when holdout accuracy meets a configured floor.
- Link Python tests to requirements and extend the spec coverage check to read pytest's JUnit report.

changes.title: Phase 4: Event-driven inference
changes.why: There is a registered model but no way to use it. Inference has to work the way the rest of the platform will: services that never call each other directly, work that survives a worker crashing mid-job, and events other services can react to (the drift monitor, later). The registry also writes events to its outbox but nothing publishes them, so no other service can learn that a version was promoted.
changes.what_changes:
- Define the JetStream streams and the job-status key-value bucket in code, created idempotently at service startup.
- Publish the registry's outbox to JetStream: each record once per message id, then marked published.
- Add `spotter.v1.InferenceService` to the gateway (gRPC and REST): submit an image for a model and get a job id; look the job up later. The gateway stores the image in the object store, records the job as pending, and publishes an `InferenceRequested` event.
- Turn the Python worker into an inference worker: pull jobs from a durable JetStream consumer, load the model's production version (verifying the artifact's checksum), classify the image, record exactly one result per job, publish an `InferenceCompleted` event, and acknowledge. Transient failures are retried with a delay; jobs that can never succeed are failed, recorded, and sent to a dead-letter subject.
- The worker reloads its model when a version of its model enters or leaves production.
- Add `spotterctl infer <image>` to submit an image and wait for the result.

changes.title: Phase 5: Observability
changes.why: An inference request now crosses four processes (client, gateway, JetStream, worker) and a registry event crosses a database transaction and a relay before a worker reacts to it. When something is slow or fails, logs from each process can't be lined up. Operators need one trace per request across every hop, and rate, error, and duration metrics for each service, before later changes add more services and failure modes.
changes.what_changes:
- Add OpenTelemetry tracing to the registry, the gateway, and the worker. Each continues an incoming trace or starts one, and exports spans over OTLP when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set (no-op otherwise).
- Propagate W3C trace context across gRPC and HTTP (standard instrumentation) and across NATS (in message headers): gateway → `inference.requested` → worker → `inference.completed`.
- Carry trace context through the registry's outbox: the context active when a change is written is stored with its event and attached when the relay publishes it.
- Expose Prometheus metrics at `GET /metrics` on every service: request rate, errors, and duration for gRPC and HTTP; the worker's job outcomes, inference time, and its consumer's pending messages.
- Add Jaeger (trace UI) and Prometheus (metrics) to the local Compose stack, configured in the repository.

changes.title: Phase 6: Optimization
changes.why: The model is accurate, but nobody has measured how fast it is, what it would cost to make it faster, or how the whole system behaves under load. National-security deployments often run on constrained or edge hardware, so the platform must be able to produce a smaller, faster model, prove what accuracy it gives up, and serve it — and every claim about speed must come from a measurement, not an estimate.
changes.what_changes:
- Add `spotter-optimize`: export a registered PyTorch version to ONNX, check the export against PyTorch on every holdout image, quantize it to int8 (static, calibrated on training images), measure holdout accuracy and latency for each variant at several batch sizes, and write a dated benchmark report.
- Publish the ONNX variants as content-addressed artifacts and register them as new versions with their own holdout metrics. A quantized version is validated only if its accuracy loss stays within a configured tolerance.
- The worker serves `onnx` versions through ONNX Runtime as well as `pytorch` versions through PyTorch.
- Add `spotterload`, a Go load generator that drives the gateway at a set concurrency for a set duration and reports throughput and end-to-end latency percentiles, timing each job from submission to its completion event.

changes.title: Phase 7: Drift monitor
changes.why: A deployed model degrades silently when the images it sees stop resembling the ones it was trained on — a sensor change, haze, night passes, compression. Labels arrive late or never, so accuracy can't be watched directly. The platform needs to notice, from unlabeled traffic, that inputs or the model's confidence have shifted away from the training distribution, and announce it as an event other services (and later, retraining) can act on.
changes.what_changes:
- Every published model version carries a `reference.json`: per-image features (per-channel brightness, contrast, model confidence) computed over the validation split. The trainer and the optimizer write it; a `spotter-reference` command adds it to existing versions.
- Add the drift monitor, a Go service that consumes `InferenceCompleted` events, keeps a sliding window of recent features per model version, and compares the window against that version's reference with the population stability index (PSI) and the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test.
- Publish `spotter.v1.DriftDetected` when any feature's PSI reaches 0.2, and `spotter.v1.DriftResolved` when every feature falls back below 0.1, once per transition, on a new `MONITOR` stream.
- Expose each feature's latest PSI as a Prometheus gauge.
- Add `spotter-degrade` to produce degraded copies of holdout tiles (darkening, blur, noise, haze) at chosen strengths, and measure detection time and false alarms.

changes.title: Phase 8: Promotion
changes.why: Today any caller can move a version into production with a generic transition, and swapping versions takes two calls with a gap between them where no model is in production (seen while promoting the int8 variant). A national-security platform needs promotion to be earned and auditable: a candidate must prove itself on real traffic without affecting answers, pass checks that are code, and be approved by a named person — and a bad promotion must be undoable in one step.
changes.what_changes:
- The worker runs the newest `shadow` version next to production on every job, returns only production's result, and publishes a `spotter.v1.ShadowCompared` event (both predictions, agreement, both latencies).
- The registry consumes those events and keeps per-version shadow statistics.
- Add promotion gates, evaluated as code: holdout accuracy within tolerance of production, shadow agreement over enough comparisons, shadow latency within budget, and a recorded human approval.
- Add `ApproveVersion`, `GetPromotionGates`, `PromoteVersion`, and `RollbackModel` to the registry API (gRPC and REST). Promotion retires the current production version and promotes the candidate in one transaction; rollback marks production `rolled_back` and restores the previous production version in one transaction.
- **BREAKING:** the generic `TransitionVersion` no longer moves a version into `production`; only promotion and rollback do.

changes.title: Retrain on drift
changes.why: The monitor detects drift and the registry can shadow, gate, and promote a new version, but nothing produces that new version. The loop the platform exists for (drift detected, a model trained for the shifted inputs, shadowed, approved, promoted) stops at the alarm.
changes.what_changes:
- `spotter-retrain` fine-tunes the newest PyTorch version of a model on the training split with synthetic degradations (the drift experiment's blur, noise, haze, and darken at random strengths) added to the usual flips, evaluates it on the clean holdout and on each degradation of the holdout, publishes it with its lineage, registers it, validates it against the accuracy floor, and moves it to shadow. It never moves anything to production.
- `spotter-retrain --watch` waits on `monitor.drift.detected.<model>` with a durable consumer and runs one retraining per drift event, recording the event in the new version's metadata.
- The Helm chart's trainer Job can run either `spotter-train` or `spotter-retrain`; an optional retrainer Deployment runs the watch mode.

changes.title: Phase 10: Dashboard
changes.why: Every part of the platform works, but seeing it work takes a terminal, `curl`, Jaeger, and Prometheus side by side. An operator deciding whether to trust a deployment, and anyone evaluating the design, needs one place that shows the events moving through the bus, each model version's stage and gates, the drift statistics, and the measured results, and that explains how the parts fit together.
changes.what_changes:
- **Gateway event feed:** `GET /v1/events` streams platform events (inference, registry, and monitor) to HTTP clients as server-sent events, decoded from their protobuf payloads to JSON. A client gets the recent past first and then live events.
- **Drift evaluations are published:** the monitor publishes a `DriftEvaluated` event on `monitor.drift.evaluated.<model>` at every evaluation, so PSI can be charted over time without scraping Prometheus. `DriftDetected` and `DriftResolved` are unchanged.
- **Dashboard** (`dashboard/`, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind): a home page that explains the platform with one recorded image's path and a panel to classify a sample tile, a live events page, a model page (versions, stages, gates, approval, promotion, rollback), a drift page, a results page built from the dated benchmark reports, and an architecture page with diagrams. The browser reaches the gateway only through an allowlisted proxy.
- **Demo samples:** a script exports EuroSAT holdout tiles and their synthetic degradations (the same functions the drift experiment uses) for the panel.
- The Helm chart gains a dashboard Deployment and Service (locally, `pnpm dev` runs it against the services on the host); CI lints, type-checks, and tests the dashboard and runs its browser tests against a recorded gateway.

changes.title: Phase 11: Failure lab
changes.why: The event-driven design was chosen for how it behaves when parts fail: jobs wait on the bus instead of being dropped, and at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers turns retries into exactly one result. That claim has been tested piece by piece, but never measured as a whole system under faults, or against the obvious alternative: the gateway calling the worker directly.
changes.what_changes:

changes.title: Phase 14: Guided demo
changes.why: The dashboard shows each part of the platform on its own page, but nothing shows the loop the platform exists for, end to end, while it happens: traffic shifts, the monitor notices, a new version is trained and shadowed, gates fill up, a person approves, and the new version serves. Showing it today takes a terminal, a load generator, and someone explaining. The drift monitor also publishes only its final PSI per feature, so a page can say *that* a feature drifted but not *why the number is what it is*.
changes.what_changes:
- **Guided demo page** (`/demo`): a scenario in steps (normal traffic, haze rolls in, drift detected, retraining, shadow traffic, human approval, the new version on hazed tiles). Each step sends real tiles through the public inference API, follows the event feed, and explains in plain language which component acted, on which subject, and why. Because the page knows each tile's true class, it also shows accuracy, labeled as something production can't measure.
- **The arithmetic behind each drift evaluation:** `FeatureDrift` gains the bin edges and the reference and window shares behind its PSI (additive protobuf fields). The demo page draws reference against window per feature and lists each bin's contribution to the sum.
- **Scenario tiles:** `spotter-demo-samples` also writes a fixed, seeded set of holdout tiles (the split's class mix), clean and with each degradation at full strength, as one bundle per variant.
- **Recorded replay:** when the platform can't be reached (a static host, or the stack is down), the page replays a recorded run of the same scenario, labeled as a recording with its date. A recording is the log of a live run of the same page, so the replay runs the same code.

specs.purpose: Defines how Spotter detects, from unlabeled inference traffic, that a model version's inputs or confidence have shifted away from its training-time reference, and how it announces the shift.

requirements.name: PSI compares a window to the reference
requirements.text: The population stability index of a feature SHALL be computed over 10 bins whose edges are the reference's deciles (the outer bins open-ended), as the sum over bins of (current share − reference share) × ln(current share ÷ reference share), with every share floored at 0.0001 so empty bins stay finite.

scenarios.name: Same distribution
steps: **WHEN** 20 windows of 200 values are drawn from the same distribution as a reference of 4,000 values
**THEN** their mean PSI is below 0.1 (sampling noise alone gives about (10 − 1) × (1/200 + 1/4000) ≈ 0.047)

scenarios.name: Shifted distribution
steps: **WHEN** every window value is the reference value plus three reference standard deviations
**THEN** PSI is above 1.0

scenarios.name: Empty bins stay finite
steps: **WHEN** all window values fall into a single bin
**THEN** PSI is a finite number

requirements.name: The KS test is reported with each comparison
requirements.text: Each comparison SHALL also report the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic D (the largest gap between the two empirical distribution functions) and its asymptotic p-value.

scenarios.name: Known statistic
steps: **WHEN** the reference is 1, 2, 3, 4 and the window is 3, 4, 5, 6
**THEN** D is 0.5

scenarios.name: Identical samples
steps: **WHEN** the window equals the reference
**THEN** D is 0 and the p-value is 1

requirements.name: Drift events describe the shifted features
requirements.text: A `spotter.v1.DriftDetected` event SHALL name each feature whose PSI is at least 0.2, with its PSI, KS statistic, KS p-value, reference mean, and window mean.

scenarios.name: Event contents
steps: **WHEN** drift is detected because brightness shifted
**THEN** the event lists the brightness features with PSI at least 0.2 and their reference and window means

requirements.name: Drift is announced once per change of state
requirements.text: Once a version's window holds 200 events, the monitor SHALL evaluate it every 50 events. It SHALL publish one `DriftDetected` on `monitor.drift.detected.<model>` when any feature's PSI reaches 0.2 while not drifting, and one `DriftResolved` on `monitor.drift.resolved.<model>` when every PSI falls below 0.1 while drifting. Other evaluations SHALL publish neither event.

scenarios.name: Clean traffic
steps: **WHEN** a version receives events drawn from its reference distribution
**THEN** no `DriftDetected` or `DriftResolved` is published

scenarios.name: Darkened images
steps: **WHEN** a version receives events from images darkened to half brightness
**THEN** one `DriftDetected` is published naming the brightness features

scenarios.name: Drift persists
steps: **WHEN** drifted events keep arriving for several more evaluations
**THEN** no further `DriftDetected` is published

scenarios.name: Traffic returns to normal
steps: **WHEN** drifted traffic is followed by enough clean traffic to fill the window
**THEN** one `DriftResolved` is published

requirements.name: Each version is compared with its own reference
requirements.text: The monitor SHALL keep a separate window and state for each model version, keyed by the version id in each event, and compare it with that version's `reference.json`. Events for a version without a reference SHALL be counted and skipped, not compared with another version's reference.

scenarios.name: Two versions at once
steps: **WHEN** events from two versions of a model interleave
**THEN** each version's window holds only its own events

scenarios.name: Missing reference
steps: **WHEN** events arrive for a version that has no `reference.json`
**THEN** they are skipped and counted, and no drift event is published for that version

requirements.name: The monitor process is configured from the environment and observable
requirements.text: The monitor SHALL read `NATS_URL`, `REGISTRY_ADDR`, `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY`, and `S3_SECRET_KEY` (required) and `HTTP_ADDR` (default `:8082`) and `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` (default `10s`), failing startup with an error naming any missing variable. It SHALL serve `/livez`, `/readyz` (NATS connected), and `/metrics` with a gauge of the latest PSI per model, version, and feature, and shut down gracefully on SIGINT or SIGTERM.

scenarios.name: Missing NATS URL
steps: **WHEN** the monitor starts without `NATS_URL`
**THEN** startup fails with an error naming `NATS_URL`

scenarios.name: PSI gauge
steps: **WHEN** a version has been evaluated
**THEN** `/metrics` includes `spotter_monitor_psi` for each of its features

requirements.name: Every evaluation is published
requirements.text: At every evaluation the monitor SHALL publish one `DriftEvaluated` on `monitor.drift.evaluated.<model>` holding every feature's comparison, the window size, whether the version is drifting after this evaluation, and the evaluation time, with message id `evaluated-<version id>-<stream sequence of the triggering completion>` so a redelivered completion doesn't publish it twice.

scenarios.name: Evaluations on clean traffic
steps: **WHEN** a version receives 300 events drawn from its reference distribution
**THEN** three `DriftEvaluated` events are published (at 200, 250, and 300 events), each listing all five features and saying the version is not drifting

scenarios.name: Evaluation that detects drift
steps: **WHEN** an evaluation detects drift
**THEN** its `DriftEvaluated` says the version is drifting, alongside the one `DriftDetected`

requirements.name: Each comparison carries the bins behind its PSI
requirements.text: Every feature comparison the monitor publishes (in `DriftEvaluated`, `DriftDetected`, and `DriftResolved`) SHALL include the 9 inner bin edges (the reference's deciles), the reference's share of values in each of the 10 bins, and the window's share in each bin, exactly as used in the PSI, so that summing `(window − reference) · ln(window / reference)` over the bins gives the published PSI.

scenarios.name: Bins reproduce the PSI
steps: **WHEN** a window is compared with a reference
**THEN** the comparison has 9 non-decreasing edges and 10 reference and 10 window shares, and the PSI recomputed from the shares equals the reported PSI

scenarios.name: Published with the evaluation
steps: **WHEN** the monitor publishes a `DriftEvaluated`
**THEN** each of its features has the edges and both sets of shares

specs.purpose: Defines how the gateway exposes the platform's events (inference, registry, and monitor) to HTTP clients such as the dashboard.

requirements.name: The gateway streams platform events as server-sent events
requirements.text: `GET /v1/events` SHALL respond with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and send each message from the `INFERENCE`, `REGISTRY`, and `MONITOR` streams as one SSE event whose `data` is a JSON object with `stream`, `subject`, `sequence` (stream sequence), `time` (RFC 3339), `type` (the fully qualified protobuf message name from the `Spotter-Event-Type` header), and `payload` (the message decoded to protobuf JSON). The SSE `id` SHALL be `<stream>:<sequence>`.

scenarios.name: Live completion
steps: **WHEN** a client is connected and an `InferenceCompleted` event is published on `inference.completed.eurosat-classifier`
**THEN** the client receives an event with stream `INFERENCE`, type `spotter.v1.InferenceCompleted`, and a payload holding the job id and prediction

scenarios.name: Unknown payload type
steps: **WHEN** a message has no `Spotter-Event-Type` header or names a type the gateway doesn't know
**THEN** the client receives the event with its stream, subject, sequence, and time, and a null payload

requirements.name: A client can follow only some streams
requirements.text: The `streams` query parameter SHALL limit the feed to a comma-separated subset of `INFERENCE`, `REGISTRY`, and `MONITOR`; without it the feed SHALL include all three. An unknown stream name SHALL be answered with 400 before any event is sent.

scenarios.name: Monitor only
steps: **WHEN** a client connects with `streams=MONITOR` and an inference event and a monitor event are published
**THEN** the client receives only the monitor event

scenarios.name: Unknown stream
steps: **WHEN** a client asks for `streams=ORDERS`
**THEN** the response is 400 and names the `streams` parameter

requirements.name: A new client receives the recent past first
requirements.text: On connect the feed SHALL first send the messages published in the last `since` (a Go duration query parameter, default `10m`, at most `24h`), in stream order per stream, then live messages. An invalid or out-of-range `since` SHALL be answered with 400 before any event is sent.

scenarios.name: Replay then live
steps: **WHEN** three events were published before a client connects with the default window, and one more is published after
**THEN** the client receives the three earlier events and then the new one

scenarios.name: Bad window
steps: **WHEN** a client asks for `since=72h`
**THEN** the response is 400 and names the `since` parameter

requirements.name: A disconnected client leaves nothing behind
requirements.text: The feed SHALL read the streams with ephemeral ordered consumers that are removed when the client disconnects or the gateway shuts down, and SHALL send an SSE comment at least every 15 seconds so idle connections stay open through proxies.

scenarios.name: Client disconnects
steps: **WHEN** a connected client closes the connection
**THEN** the streams have no consumers left from that client

scenarios.name: Idle connection
steps: **WHEN** no event is published for the keep-alive interval
**THEN** the client receives a keep-alive comment

specs.purpose: Defines the JetStream streams and key-value bucket Spotter uses, how they come into existence, and how the registry's outbox reaches them.

requirements.name: Streams and buckets are defined in code
requirements.text: Services SHALL create or update, at startup, the streams and bucket they rely on: stream `INFERENCE` for subjects `inference.>`, stream `REGISTRY` for subjects `registry.events.>`, stream `MONITOR` for subjects `monitor.>`, and key-value bucket `inference_jobs`. Every stream SHALL de-duplicate messages by message id over a window of at least two minutes. Creating them when they already exist with the same configuration SHALL succeed and change nothing.

scenarios.name: First start
steps: **WHEN** a service starts against a NATS server with no streams
**THEN** streams `INFERENCE`, `REGISTRY`, and `MONITOR` and bucket `inference_jobs` exist with the configured subjects

scenarios.name: Repeated start
steps: **WHEN** the setup runs twice
**THEN** the second run succeeds and the streams keep their messages

scenarios.name: Duplicate message id
steps: **WHEN** two messages with the same message id are published to `INFERENCE` within the de-duplication window
**THEN** the stream stores one message

requirements.name: The registry publishes its outbox
requirements.text: While running, the registry SHALL publish every unpublished outbox record to `registry.events.<event>` (for example `registry.events.model_version_stage_changed`), with the record id as the message id and the event type in a `Spotter-Event-Type` header, and mark the record published only after the server acknowledges it. Records SHALL be published in the order they were written.

scenarios.name: A transition reaches the stream
steps: **WHEN** a version is transitioned while the registry is running
**THEN** a `spotter.v1.ModelVersionStageChanged` message for it appears on `registry.events.model_version_stage_changed`
**AND** its outbox record is marked published

scenarios.name: Publish fails
steps: **WHEN** NATS is unavailable while records are pending
**THEN** the records stay unpublished and are published once NATS is available again

scenarios.name: Republished after a crash
steps: **WHEN** a record was published but the registry stopped before marking it published, and the registry publishes it again
**THEN** the stream still holds one message for that record

requirements.name: Trace context survives the outbox
requirements.text: When a registry change is written, the W3C trace context active at that moment SHALL be stored with each of its outbox records, and the relay SHALL attach it as the `traceparent` header when it publishes the record, so the published event belongs to the trace of the request that caused it.

scenarios.name: Transition inside a traced request
steps: **WHEN** a version is transitioned by a gRPC call that carries a `traceparent`
**THEN** the published `ModelVersionStageChanged` message carries a `traceparent` in the same trace

scenarios.name: Change without a trace
steps: **WHEN** a change is written with no active trace
**THEN** its event is published without a `traceparent` header

specs.purpose: Defines how the platform's behavior under faults is measured and compared with a synchronous chain.

requirements.name: A run injects one fault on a schedule and heals it
requirements.text: A chaos run SHALL drive closed-loop load for a configured duration, inject its fault at a configured offset, and heal it at a later offset. The faults SHALL be: `worker-kill` (kill the worker process without warning and start a new one at heal), `nats-restart` (restart the NATS container at the fault offset), `postgres-pause` and `objectstore-pause` (pause the container at the fault offset and unpause it at heal), and `none`.

scenarios.name: Worker kill
steps: **WHEN** a run with `worker-kill` reaches the fault offset
**THEN** the worker process is killed, and at the heal offset a new worker is started

scenarios.name: Pause and unpause
steps: **WHEN** a run with `postgres-pause` reaches the fault and heal offsets
**THEN** the pause command runs at the first and the unpause command at the second

requirements.name: Each run reports what clients and the system experienced
requirements.text: A run SHALL report requests sent, requests rejected (an error answer, whether from submission or a synchronous call), completed jobs, lost jobs (accepted but never completed by the end of the wait), duplicate completions (jobs with more than one stored completion event), p50, p99, and maximum latency of completed jobs, recovery time (from heal until the first second whose completions reach 80% of the mean before the fault), and completions and rejections per second.

scenarios.name: Lost and duplicate jobs
steps: **WHEN** of four accepted jobs one has two stored completions and one has none by the end
**THEN** the report counts three completed, one lost, and one duplicate

scenarios.name: Recovery
steps: **WHEN** completions run at 50 per second before the fault, drop to zero, and reach 45 per second in the third second after heal
**THEN** the recovery time is three seconds

scenarios.name: Never recovers
steps: **WHEN** completions never reach 80% of the pre-fault mean after heal
**THEN** the report says the run did not recover

requirements.name: Results are recorded with how they were measured
requirements.text: Each mode and fault SHALL be written to a dated JSON report with the run's configuration, the machine, and the timeline, and the conclusion SHALL be recorded in a decision record that cites those numbers.

scenarios.name: Report contents
steps: **WHEN** a run finishes
**THEN** its JSON holds the mode, fault, offsets, concurrency, duration, the report fields, and the per-second timeline

specs.purpose: Defines the gateway: the public HTTP/JSON front door that forwards to the registry's gRPC API, how it reports errors, the OpenAPI document it serves, and how the gateway process is configured, checked, and stopped. REST paths are declared in `proto/spotter/v1/registry.proto`.

requirements.name: Registry operations are available over REST
requirements.text: The gateway SHALL expose every `spotter.v1.RegistryService` operation as JSON over HTTP at the method and path declared for it in `registry.proto`, forwarding each request to the registry over gRPC. JSON field names SHALL be the protobuf JSON names (lowerCamelCase).

scenarios.name: Every operation is routed
steps: **WHEN** a client calls `POST /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{name}`, `POST /v1/models/{model_name}/versions`, `GET /v1/models/{model_name}/versions`, `GET /v1/versions/{version_id}`, `POST /v1/versions/{version_id}:transition`, and `GET /v1/versions/{version_id}/history`
**THEN** each request reaches the matching registry operation and returns its result as JSON

scenarios.name: Register a version over REST
steps: **WHEN** a client sends `POST /v1/models` for `eurosat-classifier`, then `POST /v1/models/eurosat-classifier/versions` with an artifact URI, checksum, and framework
**THEN** the second response is 200 with a JSON version whose `version` is 1 and `stage` is `MODEL_VERSION_STAGE_REGISTERED`

scenarios.name: Transition over REST
steps: **WHEN** a client sends `POST /v1/versions/{id}:transition` with `toStage`, `reason`, and `expectedRevision`
**THEN** the response is 200 with the version in the new stage at the next revision

requirements.name: Errors are returned as JSON with a matching HTTP status
requirements.text: A failed request SHALL return a JSON body with the gRPC code, a message, and any error details, and an HTTP status derived from the gRPC code: `NOT_FOUND` → 404, `ALREADY_EXISTS` → 409, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` → 400, `FAILED_PRECONDITION` → 400, `ABORTED` → 409, `UNAVAILABLE` → 503.

scenarios.name: Unknown model
steps: **WHEN** a client sends `GET /v1/models/no-such-model`
**THEN** the response is 404 with a JSON body whose `code` is 5 (`NOT_FOUND`)

scenarios.name: Invalid field
steps: **WHEN** a client registers a version with checksum `abc123`
**THEN** the response is 400 and the JSON details include a field violation for `artifact_sha256`

scenarios.name: Stale revision
steps: **WHEN** a client transitions a version with an out-of-date `expectedRevision`
**THEN** the response is 409

scenarios.name: Registry down
steps: **WHEN** the registry cannot be reached and a client sends any registry request
**THEN** the response is 503

requirements.name: The OpenAPI document is served
requirements.text: The gateway SHALL serve an OpenAPI document generated from the protobuf definitions at `GET /openapi.json`, describing every REST path above, with path parameters in JSON (lowerCamelCase) form.

scenarios.name: Fetch the document
steps: **WHEN** a client sends `GET /openapi.json`
**THEN** the response is 200 JSON whose `paths` include `/v1/models` and `/v1/versions/{versionId}:transition`

requirements.name: The gateway process is configured from the environment and stops gracefully
requirements.text: The gateway SHALL read `REGISTRY_ADDR`, `NATS_URL`, `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY`, and `S3_SECRET_KEY` (all required), and `HTTP_ADDR` (default `:8080`), `GRPC_ADDR` (default `:9091`), `S3_REGION` (default `us-east-1`), `IMAGES_BUCKET` (default `images`), and `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` (default `10s`) from environment variables, failing startup with an error naming any missing or invalid variable. It SHALL answer `GET /livez` with 200 while running and `GET /readyz` with 200 only when the registry's gRPC health check reports `SERVING` and the NATS connection is open, otherwise 503. On SIGINT or SIGTERM it SHALL finish in-flight requests within `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` and exit without error.

scenarios.name: Missing registry address
steps: **WHEN** the gateway starts without `REGISTRY_ADDR`
**THEN** startup fails with an error naming `REGISTRY_ADDR`

scenarios.name: Missing NATS URL
steps: **WHEN** the gateway starts without `NATS_URL`
**THEN** startup fails with an error naming `NATS_URL`

scenarios.name: Readiness follows the registry
steps: **WHEN** the registry reports `SERVING`, and later stops answering
**THEN** `/readyz` returns 200, and later 503, while `/livez` returns 200 throughout

scenarios.name: Readiness follows NATS
steps: **WHEN** the NATS connection is closed
**THEN** `/readyz` returns 503

scenarios.name: Stop signal
steps: **WHEN** the running gateway receives a stop signal
**THEN** it returns without error within the shutdown timeout

specs.purpose: Defines how clients submit images for classification and read the result through the gateway. Message shapes are defined in `proto/spotter/v1/inference.proto`.

requirements.name: Images are submitted as asynchronous jobs
requirements.text: Submitting an image for a model SHALL store the image in the object store, record the job as `PENDING`, publish a `spotter.v1.InferenceRequested` event on `inference.requested.<model_name>` with message id `requested-<job_id>`, and return the job id without waiting for the result. The operation SHALL be available over gRPC and as `POST /v1/models/{model_name}/inferences`.

scenarios.name: Submit an image
steps: **WHEN** a client submits a 64×64 JPEG for `eurosat-classifier`
**THEN** the response holds a new job id
**AND** the job reads as `PENDING`, the image is in the object store, and one `InferenceRequested` event for the job is on the stream

requirements.name: Submissions are validated
requirements.text: A submission SHALL be rejected as invalid input, without storing or publishing anything, when the image is empty, larger than 1 MiB, or the model name is malformed. A submission for a model the registry doesn't know SHALL fail with `NOT_FOUND`, also without storing or publishing anything.

scenarios.name: Unknown model
steps: **WHEN** a client submits an image for `no-such-model`
**THEN** the call fails with `NOT_FOUND`, and nothing is stored or published

scenarios.name: Empty image
steps: **WHEN** a client submits an empty image
**THEN** the call fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the `image` field, and nothing is published

scenarios.name: Oversized image
steps: **WHEN** a client submits a 2 MiB image
**THEN** the call fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the `image` field

requirements.name: Job status can be read
requirements.text: Reading a job SHALL return its status (`PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED`, or `FAILED`), and for a succeeded job the predicted class, its confidence, the score for every class, and the model version that produced it; for a failed job, the reason. An unknown job id SHALL fail with `NOT_FOUND`. The operation SHALL be available over gRPC and as `GET /v1/inferences/{job_id}`.

scenarios.name: Pending job
steps: **WHEN** a job has been submitted and not yet processed
**THEN** reading it returns status `PENDING`

scenarios.name: Completed job
steps: **WHEN** a worker has completed a job
**THEN** reading it returns `SUCCEEDED` with a label, a confidence between 0 and 1, ten class scores, and the model version id and number

scenarios.name: Unknown job
steps: **WHEN** a client reads a job id that was never submitted
**THEN** the call fails with `NOT_FOUND`

requirements.name: Synchronous classification calls the worker directly
requirements.text: When `WORKER_ADDR` is set, `ClassifySync` (`POST /v1/models/{model_name}:classify`) SHALL check that the model exists and pass the image to the worker's `ClassifierService/Classify` with the caller's deadline, returning the prediction in the same call without storing the image, recording a job, or publishing an event. Without `WORKER_ADDR` it SHALL answer `UNIMPLEMENTED`. A worker that can't be reached or has no production version loaded SHALL give `UNAVAILABLE`.

scenarios.name: Classified in one call
steps: **WHEN** `WORKER_ADDR` points at a worker serving version 3 and a valid image is sent
**THEN** the response holds the prediction from version 3, and no job and no event exist for it

scenarios.name: Not configured
steps: **WHEN** the gateway runs without `WORKER_ADDR`
**THEN** `ClassifySync` answers `UNIMPLEMENTED`

scenarios.name: Worker down
steps: **WHEN** the worker can't be reached
**THEN** `ClassifySync` answers `UNAVAILABLE`

scenarios.name: Unknown model
steps: **WHEN** the model doesn't exist
**THEN** `ClassifySync` answers `NOT_FOUND` and the worker is not called

specs.purpose: Defines how the inference worker turns `InferenceRequested` events into results under at-least-once delivery: which model it uses, how it retries, how it guarantees one result per job, and what happens to jobs that can never succeed.

requirements.name: The worker serves its model's production version
requirements.text: The worker SHALL load the version of its configured model that is in stage `production`, downloading its artifact from the object store and refusing to load it unless the artifact's SHA-256 equals the checksum registered for the version. Versions with framework `pytorch` SHALL be loaded with PyTorch and versions with framework `onnx` with ONNX Runtime; both SHALL produce results in the same form. While no production version is loaded, jobs SHALL be retried later rather than failed immediately.

scenarios.name: Production version loaded
steps: **WHEN** the worker starts and the model has a production version
**THEN** it loads that version and reports its id and number with every result

scenarios.name: ONNX production version
steps: **WHEN** the production version has framework `onnx`
**THEN** the worker serves it with ONNX Runtime and results report that version

scenarios.name: Checksum mismatch
steps: **WHEN** the stored artifact's SHA-256 differs from the registered checksum
**THEN** the worker does not load it and processes no jobs with it

scenarios.name: No production version yet
steps: **WHEN** a job arrives and no production version is loaded
**THEN** the job is negatively acknowledged with a delay and delivered again later

requirements.name: Each job produces exactly one result
requirements.text: Delivery is at least once, so the worker SHALL record a job's result only if the job is still `PENDING`, publish `spotter.v1.InferenceCompleted` on `inference.completed.<model_name>` with message id `completed-<job_id>`, and acknowledge the message only after both. A redelivered job whose result is already recorded SHALL be acknowledged without recording another result, after re-publishing its completion event.

scenarios.name: Successful job
steps: **WHEN** a worker processes a job
**THEN** the job reads as `SUCCEEDED` and exactly one `InferenceCompleted` event for it is on the stream

scenarios.name: Worker stops before acknowledging
steps: **WHEN** a worker records a result and stops before acknowledging, and the job is delivered again after the acknowledgement wait
**THEN** the job still has exactly one recorded result and the stream holds exactly one `InferenceCompleted` event for it

scenarios.name: Worker stops before recording
steps: **WHEN** a worker receives a job and stops before recording a result
**THEN** the job is delivered again and completed

requirements.name: Jobs that cannot succeed are dead-lettered
requirements.text: A job whose event cannot be decoded, whose image cannot be decoded, or that fails on its last allowed delivery SHALL be terminated (not redelivered), recorded as `FAILED` with a reason when its job id is known, and published as `spotter.v1.InferenceFailed` on `inference.failed.<model_name>`. Transient failures before the last delivery SHALL be retried with a delay.

scenarios.name: Corrupt image
steps: **WHEN** a job's stored image is not a decodable image
**THEN** the job reads as `FAILED` with a reason, an `InferenceFailed` event is published, and the message is not delivered again

scenarios.name: Undecodable event
steps: **WHEN** a message on `inference.requested.<model_name>` is not a valid `InferenceRequested`
**THEN** it is terminated and an `InferenceFailed` event is published

scenarios.name: Retries exhausted
steps: **WHEN** a job keeps failing transiently until its last allowed delivery
**THEN** it is recorded as `FAILED` and an `InferenceFailed` event is published

requirements.name: The worker follows production changes
requirements.text: When a `ModelVersionStageChanged` event shows a version of the worker's model entering or leaving `production`, the worker SHALL reload so that subsequent results come from the current production version.

scenarios.name: Promotion while running
steps: **WHEN** a new version of the model is moved to `production` while the worker runs
**THEN** jobs processed afterwards report the new version

specs.purpose: Defines how the system is driven with concurrent inference requests and what the load generator reports.

requirements.name: The load generator measures end-to-end latency from completion events
requirements.text: The load generator SHALL submit images through the gateway from a configured number of concurrent clients for a configured duration, time each job from just before submission to the arrival of its `InferenceCompleted` event, and report completed jobs, failed submissions, jobs that never completed within a timeout, throughput, and p50, p95, p99, and maximum latency.

scenarios.name: Every job completes
steps: **WHEN** the load generator runs against a system that completes every job
**THEN** the report counts every submitted job as completed, with latency percentiles and throughput

scenarios.name: Some jobs never complete
steps: **WHEN** some submitted jobs never produce a completion event within the timeout
**THEN** the report counts them as lost and excludes them from the latency percentiles

scenarios.name: Submission errors
steps: **WHEN** the gateway rejects some submissions
**THEN** the report counts them as failed submissions

requirements.name: Closed-loop mode bounds outstanding jobs
requirements.text: In closed-loop mode each client SHALL wait for its job's completion (or the timeout) before submitting its next image, so that no more jobs than clients are outstanding at any time. Open-loop mode (submit as fast as accepted) SHALL remain available for overload testing.

scenarios.name: At most one job per client
steps: **WHEN** the load generator runs closed-loop with 4 clients
**THEN** no more than 4 jobs are outstanding at any moment

specs.purpose: Defines the metrics reported for a trained classifier and how the holdout set is protected.

requirements.name: Evaluation reports per-class metrics
requirements.text: Evaluating predictions against true labels SHALL report the confusion matrix (rows are true classes, columns are predicted classes), overall accuracy, precision and recall for each class, and macro F1 (the unweighted mean of per-class F1). A class that is never predicted SHALL have precision 0, and a class with no true examples SHALL have recall 0, rather than an undefined value.

scenarios.name: Known predictions
steps: **WHEN** true labels `[0, 0, 1, 1]` are evaluated against predictions `[0, 1, 1, 1]` for 2 classes
**THEN** the confusion matrix is `[[1, 1], [0, 2]]`, accuracy is 0.75, class 0 has precision 1.0 and recall 0.5, and class 1 has precision 2/3 and recall 1.0

scenarios.name: A class is never predicted
steps: **WHEN** true labels `[0, 1, 2]` are evaluated against predictions `[0, 0, 0]` for 3 classes
**THEN** classes 1 and 2 have precision 0 and recall 0, and no metric is NaN

scenarios.name: Perfect predictions
steps: **WHEN** predictions equal the true labels
**THEN** accuracy, every precision, every recall, and macro F1 are all 1.0

requirements.name: The holdout set is used only for final evaluation
requirements.text: Training and model selection SHALL read only the training and validation sets. The holdout set SHALL be read once, after training finishes, to compute the metrics that are published and registered.

scenarios.name: Holdout untouched during training
steps: **WHEN** a model is trained and evaluated
**THEN** no holdout image is read before the last training epoch completes
**AND** the published metrics come from the holdout set

specs.purpose: Defines the stages a model version moves through, which moves are allowed, and the guarantees around each move: history, the one-production-version rule, concurrent updates, and outbox events.

requirements.name: Only listed stage transitions are allowed
requirements.text:
A version's stage SHALL change only along these transitions:

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `registered` | `validated`, `rejected` |
| `validated` | `shadow`, `rejected` |
| `shadow` | `production`, `rejected` |
| `production` | `retired`, `rolled_back` |
| `retired` | `production` (restore) |

Any other transition, including one to the current stage, SHALL fail with an illegal-transition error naming both stages and change nothing.

scenarios.name: Every listed transition is allowed
steps: **WHEN** a version in each "From" stage is moved to each of its listed "To" stages
**THEN** each transition succeeds

scenarios.name: Every unlisted transition is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version is moved along any (from, to) pair of stages not in the table
**THEN** the transition fails with an illegal-transition error naming both stages

scenarios.name: Skipping validation is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version in `registered` is moved directly to `production`
**THEN** the transition fails and the version stays in `registered`

requirements.name: Rejected and rolled-back versions are final
requirements.text: A version in `rejected` or `rolled_back` SHALL NOT move to any other stage. Retraining produces a new version instead.

scenarios.name: Terminal stages have no exits
steps: **WHEN** a version in `rejected` or `rolled_back` is moved to any stage
**THEN** the transition fails with an illegal-transition error

requirements.name: A transition requires a reason
requirements.text: Every stage transition SHALL carry a non-blank reason.

scenarios.name: Blank reason is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version is moved from `registered` to `validated` with the reason "   "
**THEN** the transition fails with a validation error naming the `reason` field

requirements.name: Every transition is recorded in the version's history
requirements.text: Each successful transition SHALL append one history entry with the previous stage, the new stage, the reason, the resulting revision, and the time. A failed transition SHALL append nothing.

scenarios.name: History lists transitions in order
steps: **WHEN** a version is moved from `registered` to `validated` and then to `shadow`
**THEN** its history has two entries, `registered → validated` then `validated → shadow`, with revisions 2 and 3

scenarios.name: Failed transition leaves no history
steps: **WHEN** a version in `registered` is moved to `retired`
**THEN** its history is empty

requirements.name: At most one production version per model
requirements.text: A model SHALL have at most one version in stage `production`. Moving a second version of the same model to `production` SHALL fail with a production-occupied error and change nothing. The database SHALL enforce this independently of application code.

scenarios.name: Second production version is rejected
steps: **WHEN** version 1 of a model is in `production` and version 2 is moved from `shadow` to `production`
**THEN** the transition fails with a production-occupied error
**AND** version 2 stays in `shadow`

scenarios.name: Different models may each have a production version
steps: **WHEN** one version of each of two models is moved to `production`
**THEN** both transitions succeed

scenarios.name: Database rejects a second production row directly
steps: **WHEN** a second `production` row for the same model is written directly to the database, bypassing application code
**THEN** the database rejects the write

requirements.name: Stale transitions are rejected
requirements.text: Each version SHALL carry a revision number that increases by one on every transition. A transition SHALL state the revision it expects. If the stored revision differs, the transition SHALL fail with a conflict error and change nothing. When two transitions of one version race with the same expected revision, exactly one SHALL succeed.

scenarios.name: Stale revision is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version at revision 2 is moved with expected revision 1
**THEN** the transition fails with a conflict error

scenarios.name: Concurrent transitions, one winner
steps: **WHEN** two transitions of the same version at revision 1 run concurrently, one to `validated` and one to `rejected`
**THEN** exactly one succeeds and the other fails with a conflict error
**AND** the version's history has exactly one entry

requirements.name: Changes and their events are stored together
requirements.text: Registering a version SHALL store a `spotter.v1.ModelVersionRegistered` event, and each successful transition SHALL store a `spotter.v1.ModelVersionStageChanged` event, in the outbox in the same transaction as the change. Each event SHALL have a unique id. A failed registration or transition SHALL store no event. Event payloads SHALL be the protobuf messages defined in `proto/spotter/v1/registry_events.proto`.

scenarios.name: Registration stores an event
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered
**THEN** the outbox holds one `spotter.v1.ModelVersionRegistered` event whose payload decodes to the version's id, model name, number, artifact URI, and checksum

scenarios.name: Transition stores an event
steps: **WHEN** a version is moved from `registered` to `validated`
**THEN** the outbox holds a `spotter.v1.ModelVersionStageChanged` event whose payload decodes to the old stage, the new stage, the reason, and revision 2

scenarios.name: Failed transition stores no event
steps: **WHEN** a transition fails for any reason (illegal, stale, or production occupied)
**THEN** the number of events in the outbox is unchanged

requirements.name: Production is entered only through promotion or rollback
requirements.text: The generic transition operation SHALL refuse any transition into `production` with a failed-precondition error that names the promotion operation, and change nothing. Only gated promotion (from `shadow`) and rollback (from `retired`) SHALL move a version into `production`.

scenarios.name: Generic transition to production
steps: **WHEN** a client transitions a shadow version to `production` with the generic operation
**THEN** the call fails with a failed-precondition error naming `PromoteVersion`, and the version stays in `shadow`

specs.purpose: Defines how a registered model version is turned into faster variants, what each variant must prove before it is trusted, how speed is measured and reported, and how variants are registered.

requirements.name: The ONNX export matches PyTorch
requirements.text: An ONNX export SHALL be checked against the PyTorch model on every holdout image. It SHALL be rejected unless the largest absolute difference between the two models' class probabilities is below 1e-4 and the predicted class is the same for every image.

scenarios.name: Faithful export
steps: **WHEN** a model is exported to ONNX
**THEN** the check reports the largest probability difference and the number of disagreeing predictions, and passes only if they are below 1e-4 and zero

scenarios.name: Unfaithful export is rejected
steps: **WHEN** the exported model's outputs differ from PyTorch's by more than 1e-4
**THEN** the export is rejected and nothing is published

requirements.name: Quantized versions are validated only within an accuracy tolerance
requirements.text: Each variant's holdout accuracy SHALL be measured on the same holdout set as its parent. A quantized variant SHALL be moved to `validated` only if its holdout accuracy is at least the parent's minus a configured tolerance (default 0.01) and at least the accuracy floor; otherwise it SHALL stay `registered`, and the reason SHALL state both accuracies.

scenarios.name: Within tolerance
steps: **WHEN** the parent's holdout accuracy is 0.9657 and the int8 variant's is 0.9640, with tolerance 0.01
**THEN** the int8 version is moved to `validated`

scenarios.name: Too much accuracy lost
steps: **WHEN** the parent's holdout accuracy is 0.9657 and the int8 variant's is 0.9400, with tolerance 0.01
**THEN** the int8 version stays `registered`

requirements.name: Benchmarks report percentiles, throughput, and their conditions
requirements.text: A benchmark SHALL report, for each variant and batch size, the p50, p95, and p99 latency per batch and the images per second, measured after warm-up iterations with a fixed number of threads, together with the holdout accuracy of the variant and the conditions of the run (CPU, thread count, library versions, date). The report SHALL be written as JSON and Markdown under `benchmarks/` with the date in its name.

scenarios.name: Report contents
steps: **WHEN** a benchmark runs over variants `pytorch-fp32`, `onnx-fp32`, `onnx-int8` and batch sizes 1, 8, 32
**THEN** the report has a row for each of the nine combinations with p50, p95, p99, and images per second, and records the CPU, threads, and library versions

scenarios.name: Percentiles from samples
steps: **WHEN** latencies of 1, 2, 3, …, 100 ms are summarized
**THEN** p50 is 50.5 ms, p95 is 95.05 ms, and p99 is 99.01 ms (linear interpolation)

requirements.name: Variants are registered as new versions with lineage
requirements.text: Each accepted variant SHALL be published as a content-addressed artifact with framework `onnx` and registered as a new version of the same model, with its own holdout metrics, and its `metadata.json` SHALL name the parent version and the optimization applied.

scenarios.name: Two variants registered
steps: **WHEN** optimization of version 1 succeeds
**THEN** two new versions with framework `onnx` exist, and each one's metadata names version 1 as its parent and `fp32` or `int8-static` as its optimization

specs.purpose: Defines how a shadow version earns promotion to production — statistics from real traffic, gates that are code, a recorded human approval — and how production is swapped and rolled back atomically.

requirements.name: Shadow comparisons are counted once per job
requirements.text: The registry SHALL record each `ShadowCompared` event against its shadow version at most once per job id, and report for a version the number of comparisons, the number of agreeing predictions, and the mean shadow latency.

scenarios.name: Redelivered comparison
steps: **WHEN** the same job's comparison is delivered twice
**THEN** the version's comparison count increases by one

scenarios.name: Statistics
steps: **WHEN** a shadow version has 3 comparisons, 2 agreeing, with shadow latencies 2, 4, and 6 ms
**THEN** its statistics report 3 comparisons, 2 agreeing, and a mean latency of 4 ms

requirements.name: Promotion gates are evaluated as code
requirements.text: For a candidate in `shadow`, the gates SHALL be: `accuracy` (holdout accuracy at least production's minus a tolerance, default 0.01), `shadow_agreement` (at least 200 comparisons and an agreement rate of at least 0.95), `shadow_latency` (mean shadow latency at most a budget, default 25 ms), and `approval` (at least one approval recorded for the version). Each gate SHALL report whether it passed and why.

scenarios.name: All gates pass
steps: **WHEN** the candidate's accuracy is 0.9657 against production's 0.9654, it has 500 comparisons with 497 agreeing at a mean of 3 ms, and it has an approval
**THEN** every gate passes

scenarios.name: Too few comparisons
steps: **WHEN** a production version exists and the candidate has 120 comparisons, all agreeing
**THEN** the `shadow_agreement` gate fails with a reason stating 120 of at least 200

scenarios.name: No approval
steps: **WHEN** every other gate passes and no approval is recorded
**THEN** the `approval` gate fails

requirements.name: A model's first version is promoted on approval
requirements.text: When the model has no production version, the `accuracy`, `shadow_agreement`, and `shadow_latency` gates SHALL pass with a reason saying there is no production version to compare with, so that the approval decides.

scenarios.name: First version of a model
steps: **WHEN** the model has no production version and the candidate has no comparisons
**THEN** only the `approval` gate can fail, and the shadow gates say there is no production version to compare with

requirements.name: Approvals are recorded
requirements.text: Approving a version SHALL record the approver's name, the reason, and the time. The approver and reason SHALL be non-blank, and only a version in `shadow` SHALL be approvable.

scenarios.name: Approve a shadow version
steps: **WHEN** `ana` approves a shadow version with reason "agreement 99.4% over 500 jobs"
**THEN** the approval is stored and the `approval` gate passes

scenarios.name: Approving a validated version
steps: **WHEN** someone approves a version in `validated`
**THEN** the call fails with a failed-precondition error

requirements.name: Promotion is atomic and gated
requirements.text: Promoting a shadow version SHALL fail with a failed-precondition error listing the failing gates unless every gate passes. When they pass, the current production version (if any) SHALL move to `retired` and the candidate to `production` in one transaction, with both history entries and both outbox events.

scenarios.name: Gated promotion refused
steps: **WHEN** a candidate is promoted with the `approval` gate failing
**THEN** the call fails, names the `approval` gate, and no version changes stage

scenarios.name: Successful promotion
steps: **WHEN** a candidate whose gates all pass is promoted while another version is in production
**THEN** the old version is `retired`, the candidate is `production`, and at no point is there zero or two production versions

requirements.name: Rollback restores the previous production version atomically
requirements.text: Rolling back a model SHALL move its production version to `rolled_back` and restore the version that was most recently retired from production, in one transaction. A model with no production version, or none previously retired from production, SHALL fail with a failed-precondition error and change nothing.

scenarios.name: Rollback after a promotion
steps: **WHEN** version 2 was promoted over version 3 and the model is rolled back
**THEN** version 2 is `rolled_back` and version 3 is `production`

scenarios.name: Nothing to roll back to
steps: **WHEN** a model's only production version has never replaced another
**THEN** rollback fails and nothing changes

requirements.name: Promotion operations are available over gRPC and REST
requirements.text: The registry SHALL serve `ApproveVersion`, `GetPromotionGates`, `PromoteVersion`, and `RollbackModel`, and the gateway SHALL expose them at `POST /v1/versions/{version_id}:approve`, `GET /v1/versions/{version_id}/gates`, `POST /v1/versions/{version_id}:promote`, and `POST /v1/models/{model_name}:rollback`.

scenarios.name: Promote over REST
steps: **WHEN** a client approves and promotes a shadow version through the gateway
**THEN** both calls return 200 and the version is `production`

specs.purpose: Defines how a trained model becomes a registered version: where its artifact is stored, what is recorded with it, how it is registered, and when it is validated.

requirements.name: Artifacts are content-addressed
requirements.text: A model artifact SHALL be stored at `s3://<bucket>/<model-name>/<sha256>/model.pt`, where `<sha256>` is the SHA-256 of the artifact's bytes. The checksum registered with the version SHALL equal the SHA-256 of the stored bytes. Publishing the same bytes twice SHALL produce the same location.

scenarios.name: Location and checksum agree
steps: **WHEN** a model is published
**THEN** the object at the returned URI has a SHA-256 equal to the checksum in the URI and in the registered version

scenarios.name: Republishing is idempotent
steps: **WHEN** the same artifact bytes are published twice
**THEN** both calls return the same URI

requirements.name: Every artifact carries reproducibility metadata
requirements.text: A `metadata.json` SHALL be stored next to each artifact, recording at least: the split fingerprint, the seed, the hyperparameters, the class names in output order, the code commit, the Python, PyTorch, and torchvision versions, the training duration, and the holdout metrics.

scenarios.name: Metadata is complete
steps: **WHEN** a model is published
**THEN** its `metadata.json` contains every field listed above with a non-empty value

requirements.name: Trained versions are registered with holdout metrics
requirements.text: After publishing, the trainer SHALL register the version with the registry over gRPC, creating the model first if it does not exist. The registered metrics SHALL include holdout `accuracy`, `macro_f1`, and `recall_<class>` for every class.

scenarios.name: First version of a new model
steps: **WHEN** a model is trained for a model name the registry doesn't know
**THEN** the model is created and version 1 is registered with the holdout metrics and the artifact's URI and checksum

scenarios.name: Model already exists
steps: **WHEN** a model is trained for a model name the registry already knows
**THEN** a new version is registered under the existing model

requirements.name: Versions that meet the accuracy floor are validated
requirements.text: If holdout accuracy is at least the configured floor (default 0.85), the trainer SHALL move the new version from `registered` to `validated` with a reason stating the accuracy and the floor. Otherwise the version SHALL stay `registered` and the trainer SHALL report that it did not meet the floor.

scenarios.name: Above the floor
steps: **WHEN** a version's holdout accuracy is 0.93 and the floor is 0.85
**THEN** the version is moved to `validated` with a reason that includes 0.93 and 0.85

scenarios.name: Below the floor
steps: **WHEN** a version's holdout accuracy is 0.80 and the floor is 0.85
**THEN** the version stays `registered`

requirements.name: Each version carries a reference distribution
requirements.text: Each published version SHALL have a `reference.json` next to its artifact holding, for every validation-split image, the features the worker reports at serving time — mean and standard deviation of each RGB channel on a 0–1 scale — and the version's top-class confidence. The features SHALL be computed exactly as the worker computes them.

scenarios.name: Reference written with a version
steps: **WHEN** a version is published
**THEN** `reference.json` next to its artifact holds one value per validation image for `mean_r`, `mean_g`, `mean_b`, `contrast`, and `confidence`

scenarios.name: Same features as serving
steps: **WHEN** the reference features of an image are compared with the input statistics the worker computes for the same JPEG
**THEN** they agree to within 1e-6

requirements.name: A trained version can go to shadow on request
requirements.text: When `SHADOW_AFTER_VALIDATION` is `true` and the version was validated, `spotter-train` SHALL move it to `shadow` using its current revision, and SHALL request no other stage.

scenarios.name: Validated then shadow
steps: **WHEN** training validates a version with `SHADOW_AFTER_VALIDATION=true`
**THEN** the transitions requested are to `validated` and then to `shadow`, the second with the revision read after validation

specs.purpose: Defines models and model versions: what makes a version valid, how versions are numbered, and how they are looked up.

requirements.name: Model names are unique and well-formed
requirements.text: A model name SHALL be 3 to 63 characters, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. No two models SHALL share a name.

scenarios.name: Valid name is accepted
steps: **WHEN** a model named `eurosat-classifier` is registered
**THEN** the model is stored and can be found by that name

scenarios.name: Malformed name is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a model named `EuroSAT Classifier` is registered
**THEN** registration fails with a validation error naming the `name` field
**AND** no model is stored

scenarios.name: Duplicate name is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a model named `eurosat-classifier` is registered a second time
**THEN** registration fails with an already-exists error

requirements.name: A version records a verifiable artifact
requirements.text: A model version SHALL record an artifact URI of the form `s3://<bucket>/<key>`, the artifact's SHA-256 checksum as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, a framework of `pytorch` or `onnx`, and zero or more named numeric metrics with finite values. A new version SHALL start in stage `registered` with revision 1.

scenarios.name: Valid version is registered
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered with artifact `s3://models/eurosat/v1.pt`, a valid checksum, framework `pytorch`, and metric `accuracy` = 0.91
**THEN** the version is stored in stage `registered` with revision 1 and the given metric

scenarios.name: Malformed checksum is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered with checksum `abc123`
**THEN** registration fails with a validation error naming the `artifact_sha256` field
**AND** no version is stored

scenarios.name: Unsupported framework is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered with framework `tensorflow`
**THEN** registration fails with a validation error naming the `framework` field

scenarios.name: Non-S3 artifact URI is rejected
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered with artifact `/tmp/model.pt`
**THEN** registration fails with a validation error naming the `artifact_uri` field

requirements.name: Version numbers are sequential per model
requirements.text: Each model's versions SHALL be numbered 1, 2, 3, … in registration order, with no gaps or duplicates, even when versions are registered concurrently. Numbering SHALL be independent for each model.

scenarios.name: Versions are numbered in order
steps: **WHEN** two versions of one model are registered one after the other
**THEN** they are numbered 1 and 2

scenarios.name: Concurrent registrations get distinct numbers
steps: **WHEN** 10 versions of one model are registered concurrently
**THEN** they are numbered exactly 1 through 10

scenarios.name: Each model has its own numbering
steps: **WHEN** one version is registered for each of two models
**THEN** both versions are numbered 1

requirements.name: Unknown models and versions are reported as not found
requirements.text: Operations on a model or version that does not exist SHALL fail with a not-found error and change nothing.

scenarios.name: Version for an unknown model
steps: **WHEN** a version is registered for a model name that does not exist
**THEN** registration fails with a not-found error

scenarios.name: Unknown version id
steps: **WHEN** a version is requested by an id that does not exist
**THEN** the request fails with a not-found error

requirements.name: Versions are listed newest first
requirements.text: Listing a model's versions SHALL return all of them ordered by version number, highest first.

scenarios.name: Three versions are listed
steps: **WHEN** versions 1, 2, and 3 of a model exist and the model's versions are listed
**THEN** the list is versions 3, 2, 1

specs.purpose: Defines how a new model version is produced from an existing one when live inputs drift, and what retraining may do to the registry.

requirements.name: Retraining fine-tunes with synthetic degradations
requirements.text: Retraining SHALL fine-tune the newest PyTorch version on the training split only. Besides the random flips, each training tile SHALL get, with a configured probability (default 0.5), one of the drift experiment's degradations (blur, noise, haze, darken) at a strength drawn from [0.25, 1]. Validation and holdout tiles SHALL never be degraded during training.

scenarios.name: No degradation at probability zero
steps: **WHEN** the degradation probability is 0
**THEN** every augmented tile equals the original tile up to flips

scenarios.name: Every tile degraded at probability one
steps: **WHEN** the degradation probability is 1
**THEN** every augmented tile differs from the original and from any flip of it

scenarios.name: Same seed, same tiles
steps: **WHEN** augmentation runs twice with the same seed
**THEN** it produces identical tiles

requirements.name: A retrained version is evaluated on clean and degraded holdout tiles
requirements.text: After training, retraining SHALL evaluate the new version, and the version it started from, on the clean holdout split and on the holdout split with each degradation at full strength, and SHALL record the new version's results as metrics `accuracy` (clean) and `accuracy_<degradation>`.

scenarios.name: Metrics recorded
steps: **WHEN** a retrained version is registered
**THEN** its metrics include `accuracy`, `accuracy_blur`, `accuracy_noise`, `accuracy_haze`, and `accuracy_darken`, and its metadata holds the same figures for the version it started from

requirements.name: A retrained version reaches shadow at most
requirements.text: A retrained version SHALL be published with metadata naming its parent version and, when a drift event triggered it, that event's version and drifted features. It SHALL be registered, moved to `validated` only if its clean holdout accuracy meets the floor, and then moved to `shadow`. Retraining SHALL never request any other stage.

scenarios.name: Accurate enough
steps: **WHEN** the retrained version's clean accuracy is 0.95 and the floor is 0.85
**THEN** the version ends in `shadow`, and the only transitions requested were to `validated` and `shadow`

scenarios.name: Below the floor
steps: **WHEN** the retrained version's clean accuracy is 0.80 and the floor is 0.85
**THEN** the version stays `registered` and no transition is requested

requirements.name: Each drift event triggers one retraining
requirements.text: In watch mode, retraining SHALL consume `monitor.drift.detected.<model>` with a durable consumer that allows one unacknowledged event at a time, run one retraining per event, and acknowledge the event only after the run finishes. A run that fails SHALL leave the event unacknowledged for redelivery.

scenarios.name: Two drift events
steps: **WHEN** two `DriftDetected` events are published
**THEN** two retraining runs happen, one after the other, each given its own event

scenarios.name: Failed run
steps: **WHEN** a retraining run raises an error
**THEN** the event is not acknowledged and is delivered again

requirements.name: The chart runs retraining on demand or on drift
requirements.text: The chart's trainer Job SHALL run the command in `trainer.command` (default `spotter-train`), and `retrainer.enabled=true` SHALL add a one-replica Deployment running `spotter-retrain --watch` with the NATS, registry, and object-store settings. Neither SHALL render by default.

scenarios.name: Retraining Job
steps: **WHEN** the chart is rendered with `trainer.enabled=true` and `trainer.command=spotter-retrain`
**THEN** the Job's container runs `spotter-retrain`

scenarios.name: Drift watcher
steps: **WHEN** the chart is rendered with `retrainer.enabled=true`
**THEN** it contains a Deployment with one replica running `spotter-retrain --watch` with `NATS_URL` and `REGISTRY_ADDR` set

specs.purpose: Defines how Spotter's services trace requests across processes and the message bus, what spans may contain, how telemetry leaves a process, and which metrics each service exposes.

requirements.name: Every request continues or starts a trace
requirements.text: Each service SHALL continue the W3C trace context of an incoming gRPC call, HTTP request, or NATS message, or start a new trace if there is none, and pass the context on with every gRPC call it makes and every NATS message it publishes.

scenarios.name: gRPC call continues the caller's trace
steps: **WHEN** a client calls the gateway with a `traceparent` header
**THEN** the gateway's server span belongs to the caller's trace

scenarios.name: Gateway to worker over NATS
steps: **WHEN** an image is submitted through the gateway
**THEN** the `InferenceRequested` message carries a `traceparent` header in the same trace as the gateway's server span

scenarios.name: Worker continues the trace and passes it on
steps: **WHEN** the worker processes a message that carries a `traceparent` header
**THEN** its processing span belongs to that trace
**AND** the `InferenceCompleted` message it publishes carries a `traceparent` in the same trace

requirements.name: Spans never contain image bytes or secrets
requirements.text: Span names and attributes SHALL NOT contain image data, credentials, or connection strings. Spans MAY contain ids, model names, versions, stages, outcomes, sizes, and durations.

scenarios.name: Submitting an image
steps: **WHEN** an image is submitted and processed
**THEN** no recorded span attribute contains the image bytes or any configured credential

requirements.name: Telemetry export is configured by environment
requirements.text: Each service SHALL export spans over OTLP when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, using `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (defaulting to the service's name), and SHALL run normally with tracing as a no-op when it is not set.

scenarios.name: No collector configured
steps: **WHEN** a service starts without `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`
**THEN** it serves requests normally and still propagates trace context

requirements.name: Services expose Prometheus metrics
requirements.text: The registry and the gateway SHALL serve `GET /metrics` in the Prometheus text format with request counts and duration histograms for their gRPC and HTTP endpoints. The worker SHALL serve `/metrics` with jobs processed by outcome, a histogram of time spent in the model, and the number of messages pending for its consumer.

scenarios.name: Gateway metrics after requests
steps: **WHEN** a client has made gRPC calls to the gateway and then fetches `/metrics`
**THEN** the response includes a gRPC server duration histogram with a non-zero count

scenarios.name: Worker outcomes
steps: **WHEN** the worker completes one job and dead-letters another
**THEN** its `/metrics` shows one job with outcome `succeeded` and one with outcome `failed`

specs.purpose: Defines how Spotter's images are built and published, and how the single-machine demo runs.

requirements.name: Images are built on every change and published from main
